subject: Correlation matrix for groups of a data frame

messages.author: ee1f70bd6fdb599f
messages.subject: Correlation matrix for groups of a data frame
parts:
Hello manipulatrs,

I would like to obtain the set of matrices of bivariate correlations from a data frame computed for groups based on a third variable. This seems like a good application of the split-apply-combine strategy, so I thought I'd try it with package plyr. While seemingly trivial, the output I get keeps repeating the same matrix of correlation coefficients for the groups of interest, so obviously I'm doing something wrong. After reading the help files as well as Wickham (2011, JSS), I still can't figure it out.

I'll illustrate what I'm doing with the "diamonds" data set in package ggplot2:
- The grouping variable of interest is "cut", which has 5 levels
- The input data are the numeric columns in diamonds ("depth", "table", "price", "x", and "y")
- The output I expect is an array with 5 matrices of bivariate correlation coefficients stacked on top of each other, for a 25 rows x 5 columns array.

dat <- diamonds
vars.cor <- c("depth", "table", "price", "x", "y")
cor.cut <- ddply(dat, .(cut), summarise, cor(dat[, vars.cor]))

str(cor.cut) gives a data frame of 25 obs. of  2 variables (the first hint that something is not as expected), although typing cor.cut shows this:

where the row and column names look good, but the correlation values are repeated for all groups.

With the base package I can do this correctly like so:
cor.Fair <- cor(dat[dat$cut == "Fair", vars4cor])
cor.Good <- cor(dat[dat$cut == "Good", vars4cor])
...
and so on for each of the 5 cuts, and then rbind() them together into a single array, if desired.

I also understand that the output of function cor() is a numeric array, which indicates that I should use daply() instead of ddply() -- but that gives me an even worse result. Any pointers or help is appreciated. Just would like to become more proficient with plyr.

Thanks and Happy Holidays,

Daniel

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Correlation matrix for groups of a data frame
parts:
Hi:

This appears to work:

library(plyr)
library(ggplot2)

# define the variables to retain
vars.cor <- c("cut", "depth", "table", "price", "x", "y")
dat <- diamonds[, vars.cor]

# split by level of cut into a list
dat.cut <- dlply(dat, .(cut))
# find the correlation matrix in each data subset -
# returns a list
cor.cut <- llply(dat.cut, function(m) cor(m[, -1]))

# optionally, rbind into a data frame
cor.df <- ldply(cor.cut, rbind)

Splitting the data into a list of data frames by levels of cut allows
the correlation matrix to be computed within each data subset. Column
1 of each list component is the grouping variable cut, so it is
removed prior to computing the correlation matrix in the llply() call.

Dennis
